posts.name: Craig
posts.cooked:
Sidekicks are interesting to me. It seems like comics are moving away from that, but the history of it has led to some interesting situations.

For example, Young Justice is one of the best superhero cartoons in the last few years, and it at least started as a group of sidekicks getting their own team. But the sidekick aspect was minimalised, since it was all about what they did by themselves.

That said, Scholar seems like the most likely, in my mind. It would have to be someone special, though. They'd undoubtedly have to put up with months or years of just hanging out and nagging him to teach what he knows, while John constantly rebuffed him. But, after a while, it would just naturally start to happen. Ok, I may write this story now...

posts.cooked: The problem with sidekicks in SotM is that they're hard to do from a game perspective.  As a sidekick, they should logically be weaker than the regular heros, but that makes them less desirable as a playable character.  If you add them in as a second character card for the hero (like the Sentinels), then you have a card which probably has less health and is less useful the the main hero, and you get a problem like with Spite where it's not stragically sound to try and keep the sidekick alive.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
I guess it would depend on what you mean by a sidekick.

 

If you simply want someone who admires the hero or helps from afar then that's one thing. For example, if memory serves Expat was a Bounty Hunter for a while (from her Bio I think) so she could logically have a younger individual running databases and grabbing files for her back at the home base (where would Expat stay actually?)

 

However, if you want someone to fight beside the hero... I doubt anyone would last long. The sentinels heroes seem to be more of the type to tell the kids to go home because it is too dangerous. Exceptions being Unity, Young Legacy and The Idealist because they are simply too powerful to actual stop them from tagging along if they choose to do so.

 

I just don't see many of them having the patience or disregard for allowing signifigantly weaker individuals to enter a battlefield with Spite, Gloomweaver, Apostate, Grand Warlord Voss, ect.
